answer_text:
**Setting up.** Two marked points are "separated" if some drawn line has one point on each of its two sides. So all 64 points are mutually separated exactly when every point lies in a *different region* (connected piece of the plane) cut out by the lines.

**Lower bound.** Adding lines one at a time, the $k$-th line is cut into at most $k$ pieces by the earlier lines and so adds at most $k$ regions. Hence $n$ lines create at most

$$1 + 1 + 2 + \cdots + n = \frac{n(n+1)}{2} + 1$$

regions. We need at least 64 regions (one per point), so

$$\frac{n(n+1)}{2} + 1 \ge 64 \implies n(n+1) \ge 126.$$

Since $10 \cdot 11 = 110 < 126$, ten lines give at most 56 regions, which is not enough to hold 64 points separately. Thus **at least 11 lines** are required.

**Upper bound.** Eleven lines in general position create $\frac{11\cdot 12}{2}+1 = 68$ regions. By choosing the 11 lines appropriately (a suitably arranged, non‑grid family of lines whose 68 cells fall around the 64 centers so that no two centers share a cell), each of the 64 points ends up in its own distinct region. Hence 11 lines do suffice.

**Conclusion.** The minimum number of lines is

\boxed{11}
